context: A ~30 minute sales discovery and demo call. Marco and Dana sell 'Raven', a meeting-memory product (records meetings, extracts decisions and action items, and lets you ask questions across meetings with cited clips). Lena and Raj are the prospect from Acme, an EU-based company.

participants.name: Marco
participants.role: account executive at Raven, runs the call

participants.name: Dana
participants.role: solutions engineer at Raven, gives the demo

participants.name: Lena
participants.role: VP of Engineering at Acme, the prospect

mustInclude: Acme's engineering org is about 40 people and runs a lot of meetings.
Marco sets the agenda: understand Acme's pain, show a quick demo, talk next steps.
Acme keeps losing decisions because meeting notes are manual and scattered across Notion and Slack.
Acme currently uses Otter for transcription, but it only gives raw transcripts with no decisions or action items.
Lena's biggest frustration: nobody can answer 'what did we decide about this three weeks ago.'
Dana demos Raven's 'ask across your meetings' feature answering a question.
Key differentiator Dana stresses: every answer links back to the exact cited moment in the recording.
Security objection: Acme needs SOC 2 Type II certification before any rollout.
Data residency objection: Acme is EU-based and needs data stored in the EU, specifically Frankfurt.
Pricing concern: Lena thinks the per-seat pricing feels steep across 40 seats.
Decision: Acme agrees to run a 2-week pilot with 10 seats.
Budget: Lena has roughly 30 thousand dollars a year earmarked for this, pending procurement.
Action item: Marco will send a pricing proposal by Tuesday.
Action item: Dana will set up the pilot workspace before Monday.
Action item: Lena will send over Acme's security questionnaire this week.
Raj notes that procurement sign-off can't happen until Q3.
They agree to schedule a check-in call after the two-week pilot ends.
